title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
statement:
You are given the schedule of `n` meetings. Meeting `i` occupies a room from time `start[i]` up to, but not including, time `end[i]`. Two meetings can use the same room only if they do not overlap in time. A meeting that ends at time `t` frees its room at time `t`, so another meeting may start in that same room at exactly time `t`.

Find the **minimum number of rooms** needed so that every meeting can be held.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of rooms required.

examples.explanation: Around time 13 the meetings [12,15), [11,14) and [13,16) are all running, so three rooms are needed. At time 12 the meeting [9,12) has just finished, so its room can be reused by [12,15). No moment has four overlapping meetings.
Each meeting starts exactly when the previous one ends, so a single room can host all of them.

hints: The answer is the largest number of meetings that are running at the same moment.
Sort the start times and the end times separately. Sweep through the starts, and for each start, first release every room whose meeting has already ended (end <= start).
A min-heap of end times works equally well: pop the earliest end if it is <= the new start, then push the new meeting's end. The final heap size is the answer.
